One successful algebraic-identity route, including its rank-three specialization, reached the complete-counterexample stopping condition. This is not a claim of five failed routes or of historical priority.
+
+## Exact accepted result
+
+For the rational algebra of matrix-entry functions on Hom(F_n, SL(2,C)), with J its augmentation ideal, let D_n(k) be the kernel of the action on J/J^(k+1). Let A_n(k) be the kernel of the action on F_n/Gamma_(k+1)F_n, using the integral free-group lower central series. The proof constructs genuine automorphisms giving:
+
+- D_n(5) != A_n(5) for every n >= 4.
+- D_n(6) != A_n(6) for every n >= 3.

+**ACCEPTED: COMPLETE COUNTEREXAMPLE TO THE STATED UNIVERSAL EQUALITY CONJECTURE.**
+
+The frozen proof establishes, for the rational algebra of SL(2,C) matrix-entry functions and the integral lower central series of the free group:
+
+- D_n(5) is different from A_n(5) for every n >= 4.
+- D_n(6) is different from A_n(6) for every n >= 3.
+
+In particular, for every rank covered by the conjecture's n >= 3 discussion, the two filtrations are unequal. No fatal, major, or unresolved mathematical proof gap was found. This verdict does not certify novelty, priority, publication acceptance, a degree-five rank-three counterexample, failure in every degree, or the different Andreadakis conjecture concerning the lower central series of IA_n.

All independent controls also passed. None of the independent controls imports or executes the author's verifier. The checks below supplement, rather than replace, the universal proof.
+
+## 1. Primary statement, rank, coefficients, and indexing
+
+The primary OWR PDF, DOI 10.4171/OWR/2018/2, was independently opened. Printed pages 88–89 were visually inspected using the retained rendered pages, with PDF text and current publisher-hosted PDF used as cross-checks. Its matrix-entry algebra and ideal are exactly the objects in the release. The OWR definition uses the Q-subalgebra of complex-valued functions on Hom(F_n,SL(2,C)) generated by individual matrix entries a_ij(g); J is generated by a_ij(g)-delta_ij. This is a commutative component-function algebra. It is not the trace/character algebra and not a representation-theoretic Grothendieck ring.
+
+The OWR definition is D_n(k) = ker(Aut(F_n) -> Aut(J/J^(k+1))). It states A_n(k) subset D_n(k), records equality for 1 <= k <= 4, and conjectures equality for every k >= 1. The surrounding stated rank range is n >= 3. The explicit kernel definition A_G(k) = ker(Aut(G) -> Aut(G/Gamma_(k+1)(G))) and the integral lower central series are independently confirmed in Satoh's arXiv:1607.05411v2, Section 4.1. Section 4.2 confirms the same D-filtration and Section 6, Theorem 6.3, the low-degree equality. Its Section 2 uses the same group-commutator convention uv u^(-1) v^(-1) as the release.
+
+Thus a group word first visible in free degree 5 can give failure at A_n(5), provided its component functions start in J^6. Likewise free degree 6 against J^7 gives failure at A_n(6). There is no missing plus-one in either claim. The corresponding automorphisms lie in A_n(4) and A_n(5), respectively, so the first result does not conflict with known equality through degree 4.
+
+Primary links:
+
+- https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46724
+- https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.05411v2
+- https://arxiv.org/html/1607.05411v2

+
+## 2. Universal matrix identity
+
+Use the associative bracket [U,V]=UV-VU. For a traceless 2-by-2 matrix X over any commutative ring, Cayley–Hamilton gives X^2 = -det(X)I. Put U=[X,Y] and V=[X,Z]. Then
+
+    XU+UX = X^2Y-YX^2 = 0,
+    XV+VX = X^2Z-ZX^2 = 0.
+
+Consequently XUV=UVX and XVU=VUX, hence
+
+    P(X,Y,Z) = [[[X,Y],[X,Z]],X] = 0.
+
+The proof is an identity over arbitrary commutative rings; it neither divides by 2 nor uses generic diagonalization, eigenvalue assumptions, a nondegenerate trace pairing, or characteristic-zero density. In the target graded ring every input required to be traceless is traceless. Substitution Z=[X,Y] is legitimate: the commutator has trace zero over a commutative coefficient ring. This yields
+
+    Q(X,Y) = [[[X,Y],[X,[X,Y]]],X] = 0.
+
+P is homogeneous of free degree 5; Q has free degree 6. Substituting Z=[X,Y] has weight 2, not weight 1. This is why the rank-three result is at filtration degree 6.
+
+Independent controls multiply completely generic traceless matrices with independent commuting indeterminates. P and Q vanish entry by entry. The truncation bound lies strictly above their maximum possible degrees, so the zero output is not created by truncation.
+
+## 3. The representation ideal bridge is valid
+
+Let B be an associative ring filtered by two-sided ideals I^r. For invertible U=1+u and V=1+v with u in I^r and v in I^s, the exact algebraic identity is
+
+    UVU^(-1)V^(-1)-1 = (uv-vu)U^(-1)V^(-1).
+
+Both inverses differ from 1 by elements in their corresponding ideals, because U^(-1)-1=-uU^(-1). The degree r+s term is therefore the bracket of the leading terms of u and v, and all omitted contributions lie in I^(r+s+1). This is an ideal calculation in the original ring. It does not require convergence, a completed local ring, injectivity into a power-series ring, or separation of the ideal filtration. The same argument works with I^r = Mat_2(J^r).
+
+For the tautological SL2 generator matrices M_i=I+B_i, every entry of B_i lies in J. Expanding the determinant gives
+
+    0 = det(I+B_i)-1 = tr(B_i)+det(B_i).
+
+Hence tr(B_i) lies in J^2. Only the class X_i in Mat_2(J/J^2) is declared traceless. The proof never sets tr(B_i)=0 in the original ring.
+
+For the word
+
+    w = [[[x_1,x_2],[x_1,x_3]],x_1],
+
+the exact filtered-commutator calculation puts M(w)-I in Mat_2(J^5), with degree-five class P(X_1,X_2,X_3). P vanishes in the commutative ring gr_J R. By the definition of a quotient J^5/J^6, zero class means membership in J^6, entry by entry. Thus all four entries, including both off-diagonal entries, satisfy the necessary ideal-power bound.
+
+For
+
+    v = [[[x_1,x_2],[x_1,[x_1,x_2]]],x_1],
+
+the intermediate commutators have weights 2 and 3; their commutator has weight 5; the final bracket with x_1 has weight 6. Its leading class is Q(X_1,X_2), so every entry of M(v)-I lies in J^7.
+
+This implication remains true in a nonreduced or singular commutative coefficient algebra, and does not require the claim that gr_J R is freely polynomial. Determinant relations or any additional function-algebra relations cannot invalidate a polynomial identity already true over every commutative ring.
+
+### Independent finite-quotient verification
+
+A separate implementation also evaluates the full group words, not just their Lie leading terms, in universal determinant quotients. Take
+
+    S = Z[a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i]/(a_i+d_i+a_i*d_i-b_i*c_i),
+    m = (all a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i).
+
+In S/m^N, 1+a_i is a unit, with inverse sum from r=0 to N-1 of (-a_i)^r. Thus
+
+    d_i = (b_i*c_i-a_i) * sum((-a_i)^r, r=0,...,N-1).
+
+Substitution induces an isomorphism from S/m^N to the polynomial ring in the 3n variables a_i,b_i,c_i truncated by all monomials of total degree at least N. To see both directions, send a,b,c to their names and d to the displayed polynomial. The determinant relation vanishes; conversely the determinant relation solves for d using the finite geometric inverse. All generators of m are in the ideal of a,b,c, and the assignments are inverse. This uses finite rings, not analytic arcs. There is a surjective algebra map S tensor Q -> R sending universal entries to tautological entries; the augmentation ideal maps onto J because all group-word entries are polynomial in generator entries and inverse entries are adjugates. Ideal membership in S therefore gives membership in R, whether or not that surjection is assumed injective.
+
+The independent program verifies det(M_i)=1 and M_i*adj(M_i)=I in each finite quotient before evaluating the words. It finds:
+
+- w evaluates to I modulo m^6; the degree-six displacement is nonzero, with 28 monomials in each matrix entry.
+- v evaluates to I modulo m^7; the degree-seven displacement is nonzero, with entry counts 15,18,18,15.
+
+These are symbolic exact integer calculations with 9 and 6 independent variables, respectively. They check all coordinates of the relevant universal finite quotients. The next-degree nonzero results are negative controls against overclaiming stronger membership; the accepted theorem does not need or rely on those extra nonmembership assertions in R.
+
+## 4. Integral free-group nonmembership
+
+The Magnus homomorphism sends x_i to 1+X_i in the group of noncommutative integral formal series with constant coefficient 1. Its existence follows directly from the universal property of the free group and the geometric-series inverse of 1+X_i. A filtered group-commutator calculation proves E(Gamma_r F_n) subset 1+T_(>=r): the relevant unit groups are closed under products, inverses and conjugation, and taking a commutator with an element of positive order raises order by at least one. No injectivity theorem, dimension-subgroup converse, or rational lower-central-series theorem is needed.
+
+The leading terms of the same nested group words are P and Q, now interpreted in the free associative algebra, whose variables do not commute. They do not vanish there:
+
+- In P, the coefficient of X_1 X_1 X_2 X_1 X_3 is -1. The positive final-X term cannot contribute because the target ends with X_3. In the negative initial-X term the only contribution is -X_1*(X_1 X_2)*(X_1 X_3).
+- In Q, the coefficient of X_1 X_1 X_1 X_2 X_1 X_2 is +1. Writing U=XY-YX and V=X^2Y-2XYX+YX^2, only X*V*U contributes to this target, from X*(X^2Y)*(XY).
+
+A member of Gamma_6 would have no Magnus terms of degree 5; a member of Gamma_7 would have no degree-6 terms. Therefore w is not in Gamma_6 and v is not in Gamma_7 over the integers. This is a contrapositive of the elementary inclusion, not its converse. Rational coefficients in R do not weaken or replace these integral nonmembership assertions.
+
+The independent Magnus program uses a dense coefficient recurrence on the full finite set of words, rather than the author's sparse polynomial-product implementation. Right multiplication by 1+X adds the coefficient of the appropriate prefix; right multiplication by its inverse solves new[word] = old[word] - new[prefix] when the final letter is X. It recovers every retained coefficient, not merely the two certificates. There are 12 nonconstant terms for w and 10 for v, all in their stated degrees. The reduced word lengths are 32 and 30.
+
+## 5. Genuine automorphisms and action on the entire component algebra
+
+If u avoids x_t, the endomorphism fixing other generators and sending x_t to x_t*u fixes u itself. The assignment x_t -> x_t*u^(-1), fixing the same other generators, is an inverse in both orders. Consequently these assignments are automorphisms, not merely endomorphisms inducing some truncated action.
+
+For n >= 4 use u=w, t=4. For n >= 3 use u=v, t=3. They avoid the moving generator as required. In larger ranks all additional generators are fixed. The inverse argument is identical for every rank, without a stability assumption. Independent free reduction checks both compositions in the minimal rank, the next rank, and rank 9; the written generator argument proves all remaining ranks.
+
+The component ring is generated by the finitely many entries of the free generator matrices: products are polynomial and inverse entries are polynomial because det(M_i)=1 and M_i^(-1)=adj(M_i). Hence equality modulo J^(k+1) on those entries implies equality on every element of R/J^(k+1), and in particular on J/J^(k+1). The ideal is invariant because the trivial representation is fixed by precomposition with a free-group automorphism.
+
+For the moving generator, the difference is M_t*(M(u)-I); multiplication by entries of M_t preserves J^(k+1). All other generators are fixed exactly. This establishes D_n(5) membership for the first automorphism and D_n(6) membership for the second. If the chosen action is expressed using the inverse automorphism, the kernel is unchanged; an automorphism and its inverse act trivially simultaneously.
+
+On the free-group side, x_t^(-1)*phi(x_t)=u. The nonmembership proved above gives phi_w outside A_n(5) and phi_v outside A_n(6). Their words remain nonzero in the larger-rank Magnus algebra with the same coefficients. Equivalently, a retraction onto the smaller free factor would send any purported higher lower-central membership back to the disproved one. No passage from a free-group element to an automorphism is missing.

+        return [[self.add(self.one, a), b], [c, self.add(self.one, d)]]
+
+    def word_value(self, word, matrices):
+        value = self.identity()
+        for letter in word:
+            m = matrices[abs(letter)-1]
+            value = self.matmul(value, m if letter > 0 else self.adjugate(m))
+        return value
+
+
+def matrix_profile(matrix):
+    out = []

+                by_degree[str(degree)] = by_degree.get(str(degree), 0) + 1

+    return out

+

+    data = [[[list(e), c] for e, c in sorted(p.items())] for row in matrix for p in row]
+    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':')).encode()).hexdigest()

+    return [[sum(a[i][k]*b[k][j] for k in range(len(b))) for j in range(len(b[0]))]
+            for i in range(len(a))]
+
+
+def integer_bracket(a,b):
+    u,v = integer_matmul(a,b), integer_matmul(b,a)
+    return [[x-y for x,y in zip(r,s)] for r,s in zip(u,v)]

+# A counterexample to the SL2 representation-ring filtration equality
+
+Date: 2026-10-05. Problem identifier: 30003703 / OWR-15987-013.
+
+## Statement and conventions
+
+Let F_n be freely generated by x_1,...,x_n, and let Gamma_r F_n be its integral lower central series, with Gamma_1 F_n = F_n. Put
+
+    A_n(k) = ker(Aut(F_n) -> Aut(F_n / Gamma_{k+1} F_n)).
+
+The representation ring in this note is Satoh's rational algebra R: the Q-subalgebra of complex-valued functions on Hom(F_n, SL(2,C)) generated by every matrix-entry function a_ij(g). It is not the Grothendieck ring of representations or the ring generated only by characters. Let J be its ideal generated by a_ij(g)-delta_ij, and set
+
+    D_n(k) = ker(Aut(F_n) -> Aut(J/J^{k+1})).
+
+These are the definitions in Satoh's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 2/2018, printed pp. 88-89. Its conjecture asks for equality for all k>=1, in the discussion for n>=3. The same source records equality for k<=4. The argument below disproves the universal conjecture, without using the different conjecture comparing A_n with the lower central series of IA_n.
+
+Group commutators are [u,v]=uvu^{-1}v^{-1}. Lie or associative commutators are [U,V]=UV-VU. All nested brackets have the displayed parenthesization.
+
+### Theorem
+
+1. For every n>=4 there is an explicit element of D_n(5) that is not in A_n(5).
+2. For every n>=3 there is an explicit element of D_n(6) that is not in A_n(6).
+
+Consequently the two filtrations are unequal for each rank in the stated range n>=3. We do not claim failure in every degree, or decide equality at degree 5 when n=3. No novelty claim is made.
+
+## 1. A matrix identity
+
+For traceless 2-by-2 matrices X,Y,Z over a commutative Q-algebra, put
+
+    P(X,Y,Z) = [[[X,Y],[X,Z]],X].
+
+Then P(X,Y,Z)=0.
+
+Proof. Cayley-Hamilton gives X^2=-det(X)I. If U=[X,Y], then
+
+    XU+UX = X^2Y-YX^2 = 0.
+
+Likewise, V=[X,Z] satisfies XV+VX=0. Therefore
+
+    XUV = -UXV = UVX,
+    XVU = -VXU = VUX.
+
+It follows that [U,V] commutes with X, proving the identity. This argument uses no division and remains valid over any commutative ring for traceless matrices. In particular, substitution Z=[X,Y] gives
+
+    Q(X,Y) = [[[X,Y],[X,[X,Y]]],X] = 0
+
+for traceless 2-by-2 matrices. The degrees of P and Q are 5 and 6, respectively.
+
+## 2. Filtered commutator calculation
+
+Let B be any associative unital ring with a multiplicative filtration by two-sided ideals B_{>=r}, and let U=1+u and V=1+v be invertible, where u has filtration at least r>=1 and v at least s>=1. Then
+
+    UVU^{-1}V^{-1}-1 = (uv-vu)U^{-1}V^{-1}.
+
+Also U^{-1}-1=-uU^{-1} and V^{-1}-1=-vV^{-1}. Thus the left side has filtration at least r+s, and its degree-(r+s) class is the commutator of the degree-r class of u with the degree-s class of v. Higher-order terms in either input change the result only in degree at least r+s+1.
+
+The same statement applies to matrices over a commutative filtered ring, with entrywise ideals as the filtration. Repeated application computes the leading term of any nested group commutator as its correspondingly bracketed Lie polynomial. No convergence or analytic approximation is involved: every assertion is in a finite quotient by a power of an ideal.
+
+## 3. Two group words and their representation orders
+
+Define
+
+    w = [[[x_1,x_2],[x_1,x_3]],x_1],
+    v = [[[x_1,x_2],[x_1,[x_1,x_2]]],x_1].
+
+The word w uses three generators; v uses two. Consider the tautological matrices M_i=(a_ab(x_i)) in SL_2(R), and write B_i=M_i-I. Every entry of B_i belongs to J. The determinant equation gives
+
+    tr(B_i) = -det(B_i) in J^2.
+
+Hence the degree-one matrix X_i=B_i modulo J^2 is traceless in the commutative associated graded ring gr_J R. The filtered commutator calculation implies
+
+    M(w)-I belongs to Mat_2(J^5),
+    its degree-five class is P(X_1,X_2,X_3),
+    M(v)-I belongs to Mat_2(J^6),
+    its degree-six class is Q(X_1,X_2).
+
+Section 1 makes both displayed leading classes zero. Therefore
+
+    M(w)-I belongs to Mat_2(J^6),
+    M(v)-I belongs to Mat_2(J^7).                 (1)
+
+This proves actual ideal-power membership in the rational component-function ring R, not merely vanishing on selected points, numerical approximations, or trace invariance. It does not require identifying gr_J R with a polynomial ring.
+
+## 4. The same words survive in the required nilpotent quotients
+
+Let T=Z<<X_1,...,X_n>> be the ring of noncommutative formal power series with its degree filtration T_{>=r}. Its elements with constant term 1 form a group. By freeness there is a homomorphism
+
+    E:F_n -> 1+T_{>=1},       E(x_i)=1+X_i,
+
+where E(x_i^{-1})=1-X_i+X_i^2-X_i^3+... . Induction from the filtered commutator calculation shows
+
+    E(Gamma_r F_n) is contained in 1+T_{>=r}.   (2)
+
+Only this easy direction is needed; no injectivity theorem about E and no converse dimension-subgroup theorem is being assumed.
+
+Direct use of the same leading-term formula gives
+
+    E(w)=1+P(X_1,X_2,X_3) modulo T_{>=6},
+    E(v)=1+Q(X_1,X_2) modulo T_{>=7}.
+
+These Lie polynomials are nonzero in the free associative algebra. Here is a small coefficient certificate for each, with X=X_1, Y=X_2, Z=X_3:
+
+* In P, the coefficient of XXYXZ is -1. Indeed P=CX-XC with C=[XY-YX,XZ-ZX]. The monomial XXYXZ cannot occur in CX because it ends in Z. It occurs once in -XC, from -X(XY)(XZ).
+* In Q, the coefficient of XXXYXY is +1. Write U=XY-YX and V=[X,U]=XXY-2XYX+YXX. Then Q=(UV-VU)X-X(UV-VU). The target monomial does not end in X, so it can only arise from -XUV+XVU. The polynomial UV has no term XXYXY, whereas VU has precisely the contribution (XXY)(XY), with coefficient 1.
+
+It follows from (2) that
+
+    w is not in Gamma_6 F_n,
+    v is not in Gamma_7 F_n.                   (3)
+
+These are integral nonmembership results. Rational coefficients in R have not replaced Gamma_r F_n by a rational or isolator filtration.
+
+## 5. Automorphisms and the two failures
+
+If a word u does not involve a particular free generator x_t, the assignment
+
+    phi_u(x_t)=x_t u,       phi_u(x_i)=x_i for i!=t
+
+defines an automorphism: its inverse fixes the other generators and sends x_t to x_t u^{-1}. This explicit inverse is valid because both assignments fix u.
+
+The ring R is generated as a Q-algebra by the entries of the n matrices M_i. To see this, matrix entries of positive words are polynomials in these entries, and M_i^{-1} is the adjugate matrix because det(M_i)=1, so inverse-generator entries also are polynomials. Thus if phi_u fixes these generator entries modulo J^{k+1}, it fixes all of R modulo J^{k+1}, and therefore acts trivially on J/J^{k+1}.
+
+For n>=4, take u=w and t=4, fixing all further generators as well. Equation (1) gives
+
+    M(phi_w(x_4))-M(x_4)=M_4(M(w)-I) in Mat_2(J^6).
+
+All other generator matrices are fixed exactly. Therefore phi_w belongs to D_n(5). But x_4^{-1}phi_w(x_4)=w does not belong to Gamma_6 F_n by (3), so phi_w does not belong to A_n(5).
+
+For n>=3, take u=v and t=3, again fixing all further generators. Equation (1) gives triviality modulo J^7 and hence phi_v in D_n(6). Equation (3) gives phi_v not in A_n(6).
+
+This proves both parts of the theorem. If a convention makes the ring action use phi^{-1} rather than phi, its kernel is unchanged: an invertible linear action is trivial exactly when its inverse is trivial. No action-side convention affects the conclusion.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exact controls for PROOF.md. Python standard library only; no network/files read.
+
+The general proof is in PROOF.md. This finite symbolic calculation is a
+reproducibility and transcription control, not a substitute for that proof.
+"""
+from collections import defaultdict
+import json
+
+
+def add(a, b, sign=1):
+    out = defaultdict(int, a)
+    for monomial, coefficient in b.items():
+        out[monomial] += sign * coefficient
+    return {m: c for m, c in out.items() if c}
+
+
+def mul(a, b, bound=99, commutative=False):
+    out = defaultdict(int)
+    for m, c in a.items():
+        for n, d in b.items():
+            if len(m) + len(n) <= bound:
+                word = m + n
+                if commutative:
+                    word = tuple(sorted(word))
+                out[word] += c * d
+    return {m: c for m, c in out.items() if c}
+
+
+def bracket(a, b):
+    return add(mul(a, b), mul(b, a), -1)
+
+
+def mmul(a, b):
+    n = len(a)
+    return [[sum_poly(mul(a[i][k], b[k][j], commutative=True)
+                      for k in range(n)) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
+
+
+def sum_poly(polynomials):
+    out = {}
+    for p in polynomials:
+        out = add(out, p)
+    return out
+
+
+def mbr(a, b):
+    ab, ba = mmul(a, b), mmul(b, a)
+    return [[add(x, y, -1) for x, y in zip(row, other)]
+            for row, other in zip(ab, ba)]
+
+
+def is_zero_matrix(a):
+    return all(not p for row in a for p in row)
+
+
+def variable(i):
+    return {(i,): 1}
+
+
+def traceless(offset):
+    a, b, c = (variable(offset + i) for i in range(3))
+    return [[a, b], [c, {m: -v for m, v in a.items()}]]
+
+
+def numeric_matrix(rows):
+    return [[{(): v} if v else {} for v in row] for row in rows]
+
+
+def inverse_word(word):
+    return tuple(-i for i in reversed(word))
+
+
+def reduce_word(word):
+    out = []
+    for i in word:
+        if out and out[-1] == -i:
+            out.pop()
+        else:
+            out.append(i)
+    return tuple(out)
+
+
+def group_bracket(a, b):
+    return reduce_word(a + b + inverse_word(a) + inverse_word(b))
+
+
+def magnus(word, bound):
+    out = {(): 1}
+    for letter in word:
+        if letter > 0:
+            factor = {(): 1, (letter,): 1}
+        else:
+            factor = {(abs(letter),) * i: (-1) ** i for i in range(bound + 1)}
+        out = mul(out, factor, bound=bound)
+    return out
+
+
+def substitute(word, images):
+    out = ()
+    for i in word:
+        image = images[abs(i)]
+        out += image if i > 0 else inverse_word(image)
+    return reduce_word(out)
+
+
+def check_inverse(word, moving, rank):
+    phi = {i: (i,) for i in range(1, rank + 1)}
+    psi = dict(phi)
+    phi[moving] += word
+    psi[moving] += inverse_word(word)
+    assert all(abs(i) != moving for i in word)
+    for i in range(1, rank + 1):
+        assert substitute(phi[i], psi) == (i,)
+        assert substitute(psi[i], phi) == (i,)
+
+
+def serialized(poly):
+    return [{"word": list(m), "coefficient": c} for m, c in sorted(poly.items())]
+
+
+def run():
+    x, y, z = (variable(i) for i in (1, 2, 3))
+    p = bracket(bracket(bracket(x, y), bracket(x, z)), x)
+    q = bracket(bracket(bracket(x, y), bracket(x, bracket(x, y))), x)
+    assert len(p) == 12 and p[(1, 1, 2, 1, 3)] == -1
+    assert len(q) == 10 and q[(1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2)] == 1
+    gx, gy, gz = (1,), (2,), (3,)
+    w = group_bracket(group_bracket(group_bracket(gx, gy), group_bracket(gx, gz)), gx)
+    v = group_bracket(group_bracket(group_bracket(gx, gy),
+                                   group_bracket(gx, group_bracket(gx, gy))), gx)
+    assert magnus(w, 5) == add({(): 1}, p)
+    assert magnus(v, 6) == add({(): 1}, q)
+    assert magnus(w, 4) == {(): 1}
+    assert magnus(v, 5) == {(): 1}
+    check_inverse(w, moving=4, rank=4)
+    check_inverse(v, moving=3, rank=3)
+
+    X, Y, Z = traceless(0), traceless(3), traceless(6)
+    assert is_zero_matrix(mbr(mbr(mbr(X, Y), mbr(X, Z)), X))
+    assert is_zero_matrix(mbr(mbr(mbr(X, Y), mbr(X, mbr(X, Y))), X))
+
+    # Negative control 1: changing the outer repeated variable breaks the identity.
+    H = numeric_matrix([[1, 0], [0, -1]])
+    E = numeric_matrix([[0, 1], [0, 0]])
+    F = numeric_matrix([[0, 0], [1, 0]])
+    wrong = mbr(mbr(mbr(H, E), mbr(H, F)), E)
+    assert wrong == numeric_matrix([[0, -8], [0, 0]])
+
+    # Negative control 2: one cannot silently replace SL2 by SL3.
+    H3 = numeric_matrix([[1, 0, 0], [0, -1, 0], [0, 0, 0]])
+    E12 = numeric_matrix([[0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]])
+    E23 = numeric_matrix([[0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1], [0, 0, 0]])
+    p3 = mbr(mbr(mbr(H3, E12), mbr(H3, E23)), H3)
+    assert p3 == numeric_matrix([[0, 0, 2], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]])
+
+    # Negative control 3: deleting the outer commutator loses vanishing in degree 4.
+    inner = mbr(mbr(H, E), mbr(H, F))
+    assert inner == numeric_matrix([[-4, 0], [0, 4]])
+
+    # Negative control 4: Magnus multiplication must retain noncommuting letters.
+    comm = group_bracket(gx, gy)
+    assert magnus(comm, 2) == {(): 1, (1, 2): 1, (2, 1): -1}
+
+    # Negative control 5: a deliberately false coefficient is detected.
+    assert p[(1, 1, 2, 1, 3)] != 1
+
+    return {
+        "result": "PASS",
+        "arithmetic": "exact integers; sparse formal polynomials",
+        "p5_free_associative_terms": serialized(p),
+        "q6_free_associative_terms": serialized(q),
+        "w5_reduced_word": list(w),
+        "v6_reduced_word": list(v),
+        "magnus_w5_through_degree5": "1 + P exactly",
+        "magnus_v6_through_degree6": "1 + Q exactly",
+        "generic_traceless_2x2_P": "zero polynomial matrix",
+        "generic_traceless_2x2_Q": "zero polynomial matrix",
+        "automorphism_inverse_checks": ["rank 4, moving x4", "rank 3, moving x3"],
